definition_zh: 婴儿；幼儿；初期的；幼嫩的
definition_en: a very young child, especially one who has not yet learned to speak, or relating to such a child or to an early stage of development
core_image: 襁褓中的孩子：还不会走路说话，一切才刚刚开始
scene: 产科病房的玻璃摇篮并排摆着，护士轻手轻脚地查看每一位新生儿。 The nurse checked each infant in the ward with gentle, careful hands.
sceneCN: 这里 infant 是「婴儿」（第 1 个义项：刚出生不久、还不会说话的孩子）；句意：护士轻手轻脚地查看病房里的每一个婴儿。

collocations.zh: 幼嫩产业；起步阶段的行业

derivatives.zh: 由名词加后缀构成，义为「婴儿期；初期；幼嫩阶段」
由名词加杀伐词根构成，义为「杀婴罪」
由名词加动词后缀构成，义为「把人当婴儿看待；使幼稚化」

senses.title: A very young child
senses.definition: a very young child who cannot yet walk or talk
senses.definitionCN: 尚不会走路或说话的很小的孩子
senses.example: The infant slept quietly in her mother's arms.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿安静地睡在母亲怀里。
senses.why: The Latin root means unable to speak, and a baby is precisely a person who cannot yet talk.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根的本义是「不会说话」，而婴儿恰恰是尚未开口说话的人。

senses.title: Relating to babies or early childhood
senses.definition: connected with babies or very young children
senses.definitionCN: 与婴儿或幼儿相关的
senses.example: The hospital has a special infant care unit.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院设有专门的婴儿护理病房。
senses.why: Once the noun names the baby, the adjective form naturally describes anything belonging to that stage of life.
senses.whyCN: 名词指称婴儿之后，形容词形式自然用来描述属于这一人生阶段的事物。

senses.title: At an early stage of development
senses.definition: at the beginning stage of development, not yet fully grown or established
senses.definitionCN: 处于发展初期，尚未成熟或稳固的
senses.example: The company is still in its infant stage.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司仍处于初创阶段。
senses.why: The image of a baby extends metaphorically to anything that is newly born and still fragile.
senses.whyCN: 婴儿的画面被引申到任何新近诞生、依然脆弱的事物上。

senses.title: Very young and inexperienced
senses.definition: very young and lacking experience or maturity
senses.definitionCN: 年纪很小、缺乏经验或不够成熟的
senses.example: His infant understanding of politics soon deepened.
senses.exampleCN: 他对政治的稚嫩理解很快加深了。
senses.why: A child's lack of knowledge and skill becomes a way to describe any raw, undeveloped ability.
senses.whyCN: 孩子的无知与不熟练，被用来形容任何生涩、未发展成熟的能力。

intro.en: Infant goes back to a Latin word that literally means one who cannot speak.
intro.cn: infant 的源头是一个拉丁词，字面意思是「还不会说话的人」。

items.en: From Latin infans, meaning unable to speak, formed from in- (not) plus the root of fari (to speak).
items.cn: 源自拉丁语 infans，意为「不会说话的」，由 in-（不）加 fari（说话）的词根构成。

items.en: In late Latin infans had already become a noun meaning a very young child.
items.cn: 在晚期拉丁语中，infans 已转为名词，指很小的孩子。

items.en: Old French borrowed the word as enfant, keeping both the noun and adjective senses.
items.cn: 古法语将其借入为 enfant，同时保留名词与形容词两种用法。

items.en: English took the word from French in the fourteenth century, first as a young person and soon as a baby.
items.cn: 英语于十四世纪经由法语引入该词，最初泛指年轻人，很快专指婴儿。

items.en: The adjective senses for early stages of businesses and skills developed by extension in later centuries.
items.cn: 后世通过引申发展出形容行业与技能初期阶段的形容词用法。

note.en: Watch out for words that resemble infant and for terms that live in the same childhood field.
note.cn: 注意与 infant 拼写相近的词，以及同属幼儿领域的相关词。

entries.definition: soldiers who fight on foot
entries.definitionCN: 步兵；只是拼写相近，词源其实同根，都来自「不说话」的拉丁词形

entries.definition: the period of being a very young child; an early stage
entries.definitionCN: 婴儿期；初期阶段，由 infant 直接派生

entries.definition: to fill something with air or gas
entries.definitionCN: 使充气；膨胀；只是开头拼写相近，词源完全不同

entries.definition: a very young child; everyday word
entries.definitionCN: 宝宝；日常用语，语气亲切

entries.definition: a child who has just learned to walk
entries.definitionCN: 刚学会走路的孩子，比婴儿稍大

entries.definition: a baby that has just been born
entries.definitionCN: 新生儿，强调刚出生的状态

normalIntro.en: Five links built from the real root and word family.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词根与词族的联想。

normal.en: in- (not) + fant from fari (to speak): a person who cannot yet speak.
normal.cn: in-（不）+ 词根 fant（源自 fari 说话）：还不会说话的人。

normal.en: Same root as infancy, the stage of being an infant.
normal.cn: 与 infancy 同根，即婴儿所处的阶段。

normal.en: Infantry shares the root: foot soldiers once meant the young, untried men.
normal.cn: infantry 同根：步兵一词古时与年轻未经历练的士兵相关。

normal.en: The word family grows: infant, infancy, infanticide, infantilize.
normal.cn: 词族可以展开：infant、infancy、infanticide、infantilize。

normal.en: Pair it with the opposite end of life: the infant and the elderly.
normal.cn: 与人生的另一端对照：婴儿与老人。

abstract.en: A cradle by the window, the smallest person in the house sleeping.
abstract.cn: 窗边的摇篮，家里最小的人正在安睡。

abstract.en: First sounds: the baby opens its mouth but words have not arrived yet.
abstract.cn: 第一声咿呀：婴儿张着嘴，词语还没有到来。

abstract.en: A seedling in spring soil: alive, tiny, waiting to grow.
abstract.cn: 春泥里的一株幼苗：鲜活、微小、等待生长。

examples.en: The infant reached for the bright toy above the cradle.
examples.cn: 婴儿伸手去抓摇篮上方鲜亮的玩具。

examples.en: Infant mortality has fallen sharply in recent decades.
examples.cn: 近几十年来婴儿死亡率大幅下降。

examples.en: She managed the budget for the infant company with great care.
examples.cn: 她悉心管理着这家初创公司的预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「婴富疼」——婴儿躺在软软的摇篮里，被褥厚厚的，一压就陷下去，像富贵人家的孩子被疼爱。

root: 拉丁语 infans（不会说话的），由否定前缀 in-（不）与动词 fari（说话）的词根构成；「不会说话的人」即婴儿。

sensesIntro.en: From a child who cannot speak, the word spreads to baby-related things and to early fragile stages.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「还不会说话的孩子」出发，词义扩展到与婴儿相关的事物，再引申到初期脆弱的阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one who cannot yet speak
core.cn: 核心意象：还不会说话的人

branches.en: the basic noun meaning: a baby
branches.cn: 名词本义：婴儿

branches.en: adjective use for anything connected with babies
branches.cn: 形容词用法：与婴儿相关的一切

branches.en: metaphor for a newly born organization or field
branches.cn: 比喻新生的机构或领域

branches.en: lack of experience and maturity
branches.cn: 缺乏经验与不成熟

branches.en: the life of a child and the life of a project both start small
branches.cn: 孩子的生命与项目的生命同样始于微小

intro.en: Infant is built from a negative prefix and a speech root.
intro.cn: infant 由否定前缀与言语词根构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces in- and fari generate a whole family of English words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语部件 in- 与 fari 生成了一整个英语词族。

definition_zh: 出版商；出版社；出版者；发表者；发行商
definition_en: a person or company that prepares and issues books, newspapers, music or software for sale; a person who makes something publicly known
core_image: 一间堆满校样与清样的办公室，印章落下，一本书就此成批印出
scene: 校样堆满长桌，她逐页核对页码与插图，再把封面方案递给社长。 The publisher approved the final proofs and set the print run.
sceneCN: 这里 publisher 是「出版商」（第 1 个义项：经营图书出版的公司或人）；句意为出版商批准了最后的清样并确定了印数。画面里可留意：校样、长桌、封面方案。

pos.zh: 出版商；出版社；发表者；发行商

derivatives.zh: publisher 的动词基础，指出版、发表
publish 加 -ation，指出版行为或出版物
publish 的动名词，指出版行业
同出拉丁 publicus 词根，指宣传、公众关注

senses.title: A company or person that issues books
senses.definition: a person or company whose business is preparing and issuing books, newspapers or magazines for sale
senses.definitionCN: 以编印并发行图书、报纸或杂志为业务的个人或公司
senses.example: The publisher planned a print run of eight thousand copies.
senses.exampleCN: 出版商计划印制八千册。
senses.why: The verb publish comes from Latin publicare, 'to make public', and adding the agent suffix -er names whoever makes a text public on a commercial scale.
senses.whyCN: 动词 publish 来自拉丁语 publicare「使归于公众」，加上表人后缀 -er，指以商业规模把文本公之于众的人。

senses.title: A person who makes something public
senses.definition: a person who issues or makes known a statement, a notice or a work
senses.definitionCN: 发布或公开某项声明、通知或作品的人
senses.example: As the publisher of the open letter, he took the criticism himself.
senses.exampleCN: 作为这封公开信的发表者，他独自承受了批评。
senses.why: Before printing made publishing an industry, the word already covered anyone who put a text before the public, and that older use survives in legal and formal prose.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷使出版成为行业之前，这个词已泛指把文本交到公众面前的人；这一旧义仍见于法律与正式文体。

senses.title: A firm that issues music or software
senses.definition: a company that issues recorded music, video games or software and manages their rights
senses.definitionCN: 发行唱片、游戏或软件并管理其版权的公司
senses.example: The game publisher delayed the release by one month.
senses.exampleCN: 这家游戏发行商把发布推迟了一个月。
senses.why: When new media appeared, the old book trade word moved with them: issuing copies to the public is publishing whatever the medium is.
senses.whyCN: 新媒体出现后，图书行业的旧词随之迁移：无论载体是什么，把复本发行给公众都是 publishing。

intro.en: Publisher is the agent noun of publish, which came through Old French publier from Latin publicare, 'to make public'; the word therefore names whoever turns a private manuscript into something the public can buy or read.
intro.cn: publisher 是 publish 的施动名词；publish 经古法语 publier 上溯到拉丁语 publicare「使归于公众」。这个词命名的，正是把私人手稿变成公众可买可读之物的角色。

items.en: Publicus meant 'of the people, public', the adjective behind the whole family of public words.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于民众的、公共的」，是整个 public 词族的形容词源头。

items.en: Publicare was the verb 'to make public', originally even to confiscate for the state and so hand property over to the public sphere.
items.cn: publicare 是动词「使归于公众」，最初甚至指收归国有，把财产移交公共领域。

items.en: Old French publier carried the verb into medieval use for making something openly known.
items.cn: 古法语 publier 把这个动词带入中世纪用法，指把某事公开。

items.en: Middle English publishen is recorded from the fourteenth century, at first for public proclamation rather than for printing.
items.cn: 中古英语 publishen 自十四世纪有记录，最初指公开宣告，而非印刷发行。

items.en: With the agent suffix -er the noun named the printing trade, and later spread to records, games and software.
items.cn: 加上施动后缀 -er 的名词命名了印刷行业，后来又扩展到唱片、游戏与软件。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin public stem; the near-meaning group collects other names for firms and people who issue texts.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁 public 词干上的词；近义组收其他指发行文本的公司或人的说法。

entries.definition: The act of publishing, or the printed item itself.
entries.definitionCN: 出版行为本身，或已出版的刊物。

entries.definition: Public attention given to someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 给予某人或某事的公众关注。

entries.definition: A state in which power belongs to the public and its elected representatives.
entries.definitionCN: 权力属于公众及其代表的国家政体。

entries.definition: The printing and news industry, or the machines that print.
entries.definitionCN: 印刷与新闻行业，或印刷机器。

entries.definition: A named brand of books issued under one publisher.
entries.definitionCN: 一家出版社旗下使用某品牌的图书标识。

entries.definition: A firm that moves finished copies to shops rather than preparing them.
entries.definitionCN: 把成品送到各店铺而非制作它们的发行公司。

normalIntro.en: The word is simply publish plus -er, so every hook hangs on the idea of making something public.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 publish 加 -er，所以每个记忆钩都挂在「使某物公开」这个意念上。

normal.en: Publisher = publish + -er: the one who makes books public.
normal.cn: publisher = publish + -er：把书公开的那个人或机构。

normal.en: Publicus in Latin meant of the people, and the whole family keeps that public flavour.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 publicus 意为「属于民众的」，整个词族都保留这种公共气息。

normal.en: Publication names the act or the item; publishing names the trade.
normal.cn: publication 指出版行为或出版物；publishing 指出版这个行业。

normal.en: The publishing house is the house that houses the publisher.
normal.cn: publishing house 就是安放出版商的那栋「房子」。

normal.en: A publisher's imprint is the small brand name on the spine that says who issued the book.
normal.cn: publisher's imprint 是书脊上小小的品牌名，标明这本书由谁发行。

abstract.en: Between the writer and the reader stands always someone who decides what the public will see.
abstract.cn: 在作者与读者之间，永远站着一位决定公众将看到什么的人。

abstract.en: To publish is to cross a line: before it, a private file; after it, everyone's property.
abstract.cn: 出版就是跨过一条线：线前是私人文件，线后是所有人的财产。

abstract.en: The publisher risks money on judgement, and every library is full of judgements that paid off.
abstract.cn: 出版商以钱押注判断力，而每座图书馆都堆满了押对的判断。

examples.en: She sent the manuscript to three publishers at once.
examples.cn: 她同时把手稿寄给了三家出版社。

examples.en: The publisher agreed to bring the book out in paperback.
examples.cn: 出版商同意以平装本推出这本书。

examples.en: A good publisher edits, designs and markets the whole project.
examples.cn: 一家好的出版社负责整个项目的编辑、设计与营销。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「帕布利舍」——把书稿交给出版舍（出版社）帕的一声印出来，记住 publisher 是出版商。

root: 英语 publish（出版）← 古法语 publier ← 拉丁语 publicare（使归于公众）← publicus（民众的）；publisher 即 publish 加施动后缀 -er，指以商业方式把作品公之于众的人或机构。

sensesIntro.en: The core is making something public; the senses run from the trade of issuing books, to the older sense of proclaiming a text, to the newer media of records, games and software.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「使某物公开」；义项从发行图书的行业，到公告文本的旧义，再到唱片、游戏与软件这些新媒体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a proof-covered desk where one stamp turns a manuscript into a thousand copies.
core.cn: 核心意象：堆满校样的桌台，一枚印章落下，手稿变成一千册复本。

branches.en: a print run approved at a long proof-covered table
branches.cn: 一张堆满校样的长桌上敲定的印数

branches.en: an open letter whose name is signed below
branches.cn: 一封署名在末尾的公开信

branches.en: a game cartridge stamped with a company logo
branches.cn: 印着公司标志的游戏卡带

branches.en: the same contract, once for paper and once for pixels
branches.cn: 同一份合同，一次为纸张，一次为像素

branches.en: whoever sets a work before the public, in any medium
branches.cn: 无论何种媒介，把作品放到公众面前的人

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin adjective publicus, the verb publicare, the French publier, the English publish, and the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: 这个词立足于拉丁形容词 publicus、动词 publicare、法语 publier、英语 publish，以及施动后缀 -er。

latinIntro.en: Latin left a compact family around publicus, the source of all the public words in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语围绕 publicus 留下一个紧凑的词群，它是英语所有 public 类词的源头。

definition_zh: 比率；速率；价格；费率；评价；认为
definition_en: a measure of how often or how fast something happens; a fixed charge or price; to judge the value or quality of something; to consider someone or something in a particular way
core_image: 仪表盘上按固定间隔跳动的指针
scene: 实验室的仪器每隔一会儿跳动一次，屏幕上留下一串均匀的数字。 The heart rate rose as the runner climbed the hill.
sceneCN: 这里 rate 是「速率」（第 1 个义项：某事物发生的频繁程度或快慢）；句意为跑步者爬坡时心率上升。画面里可留意：规律跳动的仪器、屏幕上均匀的数字。

derivatives.zh: rate 加 -ing，指评分、评级
rate 加 -ed，指被评为某种等级的
与 rate 同源的拉丁词，指两个数量之比
over- 与 rate 复合，指高估

senses.title: A measure of frequency or speed
senses.definition: a measure of how often or how fast something happens, often per unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 衡量某事发生频率或快慢的量，常以单位时间为准
senses.example: The heart rate rose as the runner climbed the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 跑步者爬坡时心率上升。
senses.why: Rate began as a settled, calculated amount, and measuring how often something happens is exactly such a calculation.
senses.whyCN: rate 最初指算定的数量，而衡量某事发生多频繁，正属这类计算。

senses.title: A fixed price or charge
senses.definition: a fixed amount charged for a service, a room or a unit of goods
senses.definitionCN: 为服务、房间或单位商品收取的固定金额
senses.example: The hotel charges a nightly rate of two hundred pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店每晚收费两百英镑。
senses.why: A rate is a sum fixed by agreement or rule, so the word naturally named the price set for a service.
senses.whyCN: rate 是按约定或规则定下的数额，这个词便自然用来指为服务定出的价格。

senses.title: To judge value
senses.definition: to judge the value, quality or performance of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 评判某人或某物的价值、质量或表现
senses.example: Critics rated the film highly.
senses.exampleCN: 影评人给这部影片很高评价。
senses.why: Once a rate was a fixed measure, the verb could mean to place something at a particular point on that measure.
senses.whyCN: rate 既是一种固定的衡量，动词便可指把某物放到这一尺度上的特定位置。

senses.title: To consider as
senses.definition: to regard someone or something as having a particular quality or standing
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物看作具有某种品质或地位
senses.example: He is rated as one of the best players.
senses.exampleCN: 他被认为是最好的球员之一。
senses.why: Judging a thing easily becomes placing it in a class, so to rate came to mean to regard something as being of a certain kind.
senses.whyCN: 评判一物很容易变成把它归入某一类，于是 to rate 逐渐意为「把某物看作某类」。

intro.en: Rate comes from Latin rata, fixed or settled by reckoning, from reri, to reckon; Old French passed it to English as a fixed share or charge.
intro.cn: rate 来自拉丁语 rata（经计算而确定的），源自动词 reri（计算、思考）；古法语把它作为固定的份额或费用传给英语。

items.en: Rata meant fixed or settled, of a sum that had been worked out and agreed.
items.cn: rata 意为确定、算定，指经过计算并获同意的一笔数额。

items.en: The root reri meant to reckon or think, so rata was what had been calculated.
items.cn: 词根 reri 意为计算或思考，因此 rata 就是被算出来的东西。

items.en: Old French rate carried the idea of a fixed share or a charge to be paid.
items.cn: 古法语 rate 带着「固定份额」或「应缴费用」的意思。

items.en: Middle English rate used the word for a fixed charge and for a measured proportion.
items.cn: 中古英语 rate 既指固定费用，也指被计量出的比例。

items.en: Modern English keeps rate for a measured proportion and a price, and adds the verb to rate, meaning to judge.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 rate 表示测得的比例与价格，并加上动词 rate，意为评判。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived forms and one confusing neighbour; the near-meaning group gathers words for speed, proportion and charge.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与一个易混词；近义组收表示速度、比例与收费的词。

entries.definition: The relation between two amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 两个数量之间的关系。

entries.definition: A score or judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 评分或评定。

entries.definition: Judged to have a certain quality.
entries.definitionCN: 被评为某种质量的。

entries.definition: A small rodent, a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 一种小型鼠类，另一词。

entries.definition: The rate at which something moves.
entries.definitionCN: 某物移动的速率。

entries.definition: The speed at which something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的快慢。

entries.definition: A part in relation to the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 部分与整体的关系。

entries.definition: The price asked for a service.
entries.definitionCN: 为服务索取的价格。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a reckoned, fixed amount, then splits into a measured proportion, a set price and the act of judging.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「算定的数额」开始，随后分成测得的比例、定好的价格与评判的行为。

normal.en: Rate and ratio share a Latin root meaning to reckon.
normal.cn: rate 与 ratio 共有表示「计算」的拉丁词根。

normal.en: A heart rate counts beats per minute, a rate per unit of time.
normal.cn: heart rate 数的是每分钟的跳动，即每单位时间的速率。

normal.en: A hotel rate is a fixed price for a room.
normal.cn: hotel rate 是一间房的固定价格。

normal.en: To rate a film is to give it a score.
normal.cn: to rate a film 就是给它打分。

normal.en: Rat and rate look alike but a rat is an animal and a rate is a measure.
normal.cn: rat 与 rate 形近，但 rat 是动物，rate 是度量。

abstract.en: A rate turns the flow of time into a number you can compare.
abstract.cn: rate 把时间的流动变成一个可以比较的数字。

abstract.en: To rate something is to turn a judgment into a place on a scale.
abstract.cn: 给某物 rate，就是把一次判断变成尺度上的一个位置。

abstract.en: Every rate hides a choice of what to count and over how long.
abstract.cn: 每一个 rate 背后都藏着「数什么、数多久」的选择。

examples.en: The heart rate rose as the runner climbed the hill.
examples.cn: 跑步者爬坡时心率上升。

examples.en: The hotel charges a nightly rate of two hundred pounds.
examples.cn: 这家酒店每晚收费两百英镑。

examples.en: Critics rated the film highly.
examples.cn: 影评人给这部影片很高评价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞特」——仪表上均匀跳动的数字，记住 rate 是速率、价格，也指评价。

root: 拉丁语 rata（经计算确定的）→ 古法语 rate → 现代英语 rate；同根有 ratio、rating。拉丁语 reri 意为计算、思考。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a reckoned, fixed amount; the senses divide into a measured proportion, a set price, judging, and regarding as.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「经计算而确定的数额」；义项分为测得的比例、定好的价格、评判，以及把……看作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a meter ticking at fixed intervals, its numbers even and regular.
core.cn: 核心意象：按固定间隔跳动的仪表，数字均匀而规律。

branches.en: a meter ticking at a steady interval
branches.cn: 按固定间隔跳动的仪表

branches.en: a price card on a hotel desk
branches.cn: 酒店柜台上的价目牌

branches.en: critics giving a film a score
branches.cn: 影评人给电影打分

branches.en: a label pinned on a person
branches.cn: 贴在一个人身上的标签

branches.en: a measured amount and a measured price
branches.cn: 被计量的数量与被计定的价格

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built with English suffixes, a prefix and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由英语后缀、一个前缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin rata, fixed by reckoning, and the verb reri, to reckon, are the recorded sources of the root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rata（经计算而确定）与动词 reri（计算）是这个词根有记录可考的来源。

definition_zh: 方面；层面；外观；样子；（语法）体；朝向
definition_en: one side of a matter, the appearance of something, a grammatical category of verbs, or the position of a planet
core_image: 同一座房子，从不同角度看到不同的面
scene: 同一座老宅，站在街上看到的是斑驳的墙面，绕到后院却是新修的花园。 We must consider every aspect of the plan before we vote.
sceneCN: 这里 aspect 是「方面、层面」（第 1 个义项：一件事的某一个侧面）；句意为「投票前我们必须考虑这个计划的每个方面」。画面中有老宅的正面、后院与新修的花园。

pos.zh: 名词：方面；层面；外观；样子；（语法）体；朝向

derivatives.zh: 由 aspect 加 -ual 构成，义为「（语法）体的」
由 aspectual 加 -ity 构成，义为「体性」，语言学术语

senses.title: One side of a matter
senses.definition: one particular part or side of a situation, problem, or subject
senses.definitionCN: 情况、问题或主题中某一个特定的部分或侧面
senses.example: We must consider every aspect of the plan before we vote.
senses.exampleCN: 投票前我们必须考虑这个计划的每个方面。
senses.why: Latin aspectus meant a look or a view, and a matter seen from one angle shows one of its faces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aspectus 意为「看、视角」，一件事从某个角度看，就露出它的一个面。

senses.title: The look of something
senses.definition: the appearance of a person, place, or thing, especially as it seems at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 人、地方或事物的外貌，尤指某一时刻给人的印象
senses.example: The garden took on a gloomy aspect under the grey sky.
senses.exampleCN: 灰蒙蒙的天空下，花园显出一副阴沉的样子。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: aspect is simply what a thing looks like when you face it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：aspect 就是当你面对某物时它看上去的样子。

senses.title: A grammatical category
senses.definition: a verb category showing how an action unfolds in time, such as simple, progressive, or perfect
senses.definitionCN: 动词范畴，表示动作在时间中如何展开，如一般、进行、完成
senses.example: English marks aspect with forms such as is running.
senses.exampleCN: 英语用 is running 这类形式来标记「体」。
senses.why: Grammarians borrowed the word for a view: an action is seen from a particular angle in time.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家借用了「视角」这个词：动作在时间中被从某个角度观看。

senses.title: A position of the stars
senses.definition: the position of a planet or the stars in relation to one another, especially in astrology
senses.definitionCN: 行星或星辰彼此之间的相对位置，尤用于占星
senses.example: The astrologer studied the aspect of Mars and Venus.
senses.exampleCN: 占星师研究了火星与金星的方位关系。
senses.why: Planets face each other at certain angles, and each angle is a way of looking across the sky.
senses.whyCN: 行星以特定角度彼此相望，每个角度都是一种横看天空的方式。

intro.en: Aspect comes from a Latin verb meaning to look at, and every sense is a way of looking at something.
intro.cn: aspect 来自一个意为「观看」的拉丁动词，每个义项都是一种看事物的方式。

items.en: The root 「*speḱ-」 meant 'to see, look', and it stands behind many seeing words in Latin and Greek.
items.cn: 词根「*speḱ-」意为「看、观看」，拉丁语与希腊语中许多表示「看」的词都由它而来。

items.en: Aspicere, from ad- 'to' plus specere 'to look', meant 'to look at, observe'.
items.cn: aspicere 由 ad-「向」加 specere「看」构成，意为「注视、观察」。

items.en: Aspectus meant 'a look, a view, appearance', and could also name the position of a heavenly body.
items.cn: aspectus 意为「一瞥、视角、外观」，也能指天体的方位。

items.en: Old French aspect kept both the appearance sense and the astronomical one.
items.cn: 古法语 aspect 同时保留「外观」义与天象义。

items.en: English used aspect for appearance and for the stars, and the 'side of a matter' sense came later.
items.cn: 英语最早用 aspect 指外观与星辰，后来才发展出「事情的方面」这一义。

items.en: Grammar added the verb sense in the nineteenth century, viewing an action from an angle in time.
items.cn: 语法学在十九世纪添上动词「体」义，从时间中的某个角度观看动作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the Latin seeing root; the near-meaning group gathers sides, facets and appearances.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁「看」词根的词；近义组收表示侧面、层面与外观的词。

entries.definition: To look at something closely to check its condition.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细查看某物以检查其状况。

entries.definition: A striking public display or sight.
entries.definitionCN: 引人注目的公开场面或景象。

entries.definition: Admiration for someone, or a particular point or detail.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人的敬意，或某个具体的方面、细节。

entries.definition: One part or face of a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 事情的一个部分或一个面。

entries.definition: One of the many sides of a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 一个主题众多侧面中的一个。

entries.definition: A particular way of viewing a situation.
entries.definitionCN: 看待某一情况的特定角度。

entries.definition: The way something looks to the eye.
entries.definitionCN: 某物呈现在眼中的样子。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from one house seen from two sides to a gloomy garden, a verb form and the stars.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从一座房子从两边看，走到阴沉的花园、动词形式与星辰。

normal.en: One house, many faces: each angle is an aspect.
normal.cn: 一座房子有许多面：每个角度都是一个 aspect。

normal.en: The same problem seen from the side shows another aspect.
normal.cn: 同一个问题从侧面看，会露出另一个方面。

normal.en: The garden's aspect under grey sky is gloomy.
normal.cn: 灰天下花园的 aspect 是阴沉的。

normal.en: Grammar views an action from an angle in time.
normal.cn: 语法从时间中的某个角度观看动作。

normal.en: Planets face each other at an aspect.
normal.cn: 行星以某个方位彼此相望。

abstract.en: Every sense is a way of looking at something.
abstract.cn: 每一个义项都是看某样东西的一种方式。

abstract.en: A face, a side and a view share one root.
abstract.cn: 面容、侧面与视角共用一个词根。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from space to grammar to the sky.
abstract.cn: 这个词从空间滑到语法，再滑到天空。

examples.en: We must consider every aspect of the plan before we vote.
examples.cn: 投票前我们必须考虑这个计划的每个方面。

examples.en: The garden took on a gloomy aspect under the grey sky.
examples.cn: 灰蒙蒙的天空下，花园显出一副阴沉的样子。

examples.en: The astrologer studied the aspect of Mars and Venus.
examples.cn: 占星师研究了火星与金星的方位关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿斯佩克特」——阿斯佩克特绕到房子背面，看到另一个面：方面

root: aspect 来自拉丁语 aspicere「注视」，由 ad-「向」加 specere「看」构成；其名词 aspectus 意为「一瞥、视角、外观」，也能指天体方位。因此它先指「样子、外观」，后指「从某一角度看到的一面」，即事情的方面；语法学又借它表示「体」——从时间中的某个角度观看动作；占星术里的 aspect 则是行星彼此的方位。词根 specere 还留在 inspect、spectacle 里。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses are four ways of looking: at one side of a matter, at a thing's appearance, at how a verb unfolds, and at the stars' angle.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项是四种看的方式：看事情的一个侧面、看一个事物的样子、看动词如何展开，以及看星辰的方位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one old house showing a weathered wall from the street and a new garden from the back.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一座老宅，从街上看到斑驳的墙，从后院看到新修的花园。

branches.en: THE MATTER LINE: a complex thing is considered one side at a time.
branches.cn: 事情线：复杂的事物被一个面一个面地看。

branches.en: THE FACE LINE: the oldest sense, simply how a thing looks.
branches.cn: 面容线：最古老的义项，就是某物看上去的样子。

branches.en: THE GRAMMAR LINE: an action is viewed from an angle in time.
branches.cn: 语法线：动作被从时间中的某个角度观看。

branches.en: THE SKY LINE: planets face each other at fixed angles.
branches.cn: 天空线：行星以固定角度彼此相望。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY LINE: the side of a problem and the look of a place are both aspects.
branches.cn: 日常线：问题的侧面与地方的样子，都是 aspect。

intro.en: Aspect is a Latin noun; its family adds -ual and -ity, and the root specere also builds inspect and spectacle.
intro.cn: aspect 是拉丁名词，词族加 -ual 与 -ity；词根 specere 还构成 inspect 与 spectacle。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root specere 'to look' also gave English inspect, spectacle and perspective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 specere「看」还给英语留下了 inspect、spectacle 与 perspective。

items.meaning: a look, a view, one side of a thing
items.meaningCN: 一看、视角、事物的一个侧面
items.example: The financial aspect worries them most.
items.exampleCN: 财务方面最让他们担心。

items.example: The report covers all aspects of the case.
items.exampleCN: 报告涵盖了这个案子的各个方面。
这篇论文研究「体」的意义。

items.meaningCN: 引人注目的景象或场面
items.example: The fireworks were a fine spectacle.

items.meaning: a point of view, or the art of showing depth
items.meaningCN: 视角，或表现纵深的透视法
items.example: Try seeing it from her perspective.
items.exampleCN: 试着从她的角度看这件事。

items.meaning: the proportion of width to height
items.example: The film uses a wide aspect ratio.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片采用宽幅比例。

latinEntries.example: The parade was quite a spectacle.
They inspect the goods on arrival.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 货物到达时他们会检查。

definition_zh: 关节；接缝；共同的；合办的
definition_en: a place where two parts of a body or structure are connected, or something shared by two or more people
core_image: 两根木条在拐角处被一个榫头接住，那儿可以弯
scene: 木工把两根长条拼成一张矮凳，接头处特意留了一点松动。 The table is held together by wooden joints, no nails.
sceneCN: 这里 joint 是「接缝」（第 2 个义项：两个构件相接的部位），句意为这张桌子靠木接缝拼成，不用一根钉子。画面里的物件：木条、榫头、矮凳。

pos.zh: 名词：关节；接缝；大块烤肉

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「共同地」
同词根的动词，义为「连接；加入」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「有关节的」
加前缀 dis- 构成，义为「脱节的；不连贯的」

senses.title: A body joint
senses.definition: the place where two bones meet and allow movement
senses.definitionCN: 两块骨头相接并能活动的地方
senses.example: He hurt the joint of his thumb in the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他的拇指关节被门夹伤了。
senses.why: Anatomy used the word first in English, for the points where bones meet.
senses.whyCN: 英语里最先用它的就是解剖，指骨头相接的地方。

senses.title: A place where parts meet
senses.definition: the point where two pieces of wood or metal are fitted together
senses.definitionCN: 两块木头或金属相嵌合的地方
senses.example: The pipe leaked at the joint near the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 那根管子靠墙的接头处漏水。
senses.why: Carpenters and plumbers borrowed the same word for made joins.
senses.whyCN: 木匠和水管工借同一个词来说人造的接合。

senses.title: Shared by two or more
senses.definition: made or held together by two or more parties
senses.definitionCN: 由两方或多方一起做或一起持有的
senses.example: They run a joint shop and split the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他们合开一家店，房租分摊。
senses.why: The adjective sense moves from physical joining to shared ownership.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义从物理连接挪到共同拥有。

senses.title: A large cut of meat
senses.definition: a piece of meat for roasting, usually with the bone still in
senses.definitionCN: 用于烤制的一块肉，通常带骨
senses.example: Sunday meant a joint of beef and a long table.
senses.exampleCN: 星期天意味着一条烤牛腿和一张长餐桌。
senses.why: A roast joint is the piece carved at the table, where the family joins.
senses.whyCN: 烤大块肉是要在桌上切开的那块，一家人正是在那儿连起来。

intro.en: Joint comes from Latin junctus, "joined", the past participle of jungere, "to join".
intro.cn: joint 来自拉丁语 junctus「已连接的」，是 jungere「连接」的过去分词。

items.en: jungere meant "to join, to yoke together".
items.cn: jungere 意为「连接、套上轭」。

items.en: The past participle junctus meant "joined".
items.cn: 过去分词 junctus 意为「已连接的」。

items.en: French turned it into joint, naming the place of meeting.
items.cn: 法语把它变成 joint，指相接之处。

items.en: Middle English used joint for bones and for carpentry.
items.cn: 中古英语用 joint 指骨头与木作。

items.en: The shared sense grew from "joined together" into business use.
items.cn: 「连在一起」逐渐扩展出商务上的「共同」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the join- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for connections and sharing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 join- 词干；近义组收表示连接与共有的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to connect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「连接」，同词根。

entries.definition: Together, by two or more parties.
entries.definitionCN: 副词义为「共同地」，同族词。

entries.definition: Lacking connection or order.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「不连贯的」，加前缀 dis-。

entries.definition: A line where two pieces are sewn or joined.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「缝」，多指布料。

entries.definition: Used or held by more than one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「共有的」，偏所有权。

entries.definition: Felt or done by each towards the other.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「相互的」，偏态度。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the word at a point where two things touch.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它放在两物相触的那一点上。

normal.en: jungere means join, and junctus means joined.
normal.cn: jungere 是连接，junctus 是已连接。

normal.en: A joint is where the joining shows.
normal.cn: joint 就是接合显现出来的地方。

normal.en: Remove the joint and the parts fall apart.
normal.cn: 把这个接点去掉，部件就散了。

normal.en: Bones, planks, and bank accounts all have joints.
normal.cn: 骨头、木板、银行账户都有「接头」。

normal.en: Jointly means the two are joined in acting.
normal.cn: jointly 就是两方连着一起做。

abstract.en: A joint is the hinge where one thing becomes two.
abstract.cn: 接缝是一物分成两物的那处铰链。

abstract.en: Bodies and agreements both fail at the joint.
abstract.cn: 身体和协议，都容易在连接处出问题。

abstract.en: Shared work bends better than separate work.
abstract.cn: 共同的事，比分开的事更会弯。

examples.en: His ankle joint still aches after the fall.
examples.cn: 摔倒之后他的踝关节还疼。

examples.en: The chair needs a new wooden joint at the back.
examples.cn: 这把椅子的后部需要换一个木接缝。

examples.en: The two cities opened a joint fire service last year.
examples.cn: 两座城市去年开设了合办的消防服务。

dict_mnemonic.text: join（连接）+ t —— 两块东西连起来的那一点

root: 拉丁语 jungere「连接」→ junctus「已连接的」→ 古法语 joint → 中古英语 joint。同族有 join、jointly、junction、conjunction。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: a bone joint, a fitted seam, something shared, and a cut of meat.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：骨头关节、构件接缝、共同持有的，以及一大块肉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hinge where two pieces meet and can move.
core.cn: 核心意象：两件东西相接并能活动的那处铰链。

branches.en: THE BODY: bones meeting where movement happens.
branches.cn: 身体这条线：能活动的骨相接处。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: wood and pipe fitted at a seam.
branches.cn: 手艺这条线：木头与管子在缝处相嵌。

branches.en: THE DEAL: two parties holding one thing.
branches.cn: 交易这条线：两方持有一物。

branches.en: THE TABLE: a joint of meat at a shared meal.
branches.cn: 餐桌这条线：一顿共餐上的一大块肉。

branches.en: THE LINK: all senses are a place where two become one.
branches.cn: 连接这条线：所有义项都是两物合一之处。

intro.cn: joint 是词根 joining- 加拉丁过去分词词尾 -t，整词直接从法语借来。

latinIntro.en: Latin jungere and junctus are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jungere 与 junctus 均有记载。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 junction 与 adjoin。

definition_zh: 解决；决心；决定
definition_en: to solve a problem, or to decide firmly to do something
core_image: 把一团乱麻一根根解开，直到线变得笔直
scene: 两家人坐下来谈了一个下午，终于把多年的地界纠纷解决了。 The two families sat down for an afternoon and finally resolved their long dispute over the boundary.
sceneCN: 这里 resolve 是「解决」（第 1 个义项：把问题处理掉）；句意：两家人坐了一个下午，终于解决了多年的地界纠纷。

derivatives.zh: 决心；决议；解决
下定决心的
坚决的；果断的

senses.title: To solve a problem or end a dispute
senses.definition: to find an answer to a problem or bring a disagreement to an end
senses.definitionCN: 为问题找到答案，或结束分歧
senses.example: The two families resolved their dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 两家人解决了他们的争端。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to loosen, and a solved problem is a loosened knot.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为松开，被解决的问题就是被解开的结。

senses.title: To decide firmly
senses.definition: to make a firm decision to do something
senses.definitionCN: 坚定决定去做某事
senses.example: She resolved to speak to him that evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她决心那天晚上和他谈一谈。
senses.why: A mind that stops wavering has settled, or resolved itself, on one course.
senses.whyCN: 不再摇摆的心思就「定」在了一条路上。

senses.title: To separate into parts
senses.definition: to break down or change into separate parts, used in technical description
senses.definitionCN: 分解或转变为不同部分，用于技术描写
senses.example: The mixture resolved into two clear layers.
senses.exampleCN: 混合物分成了两层清澈的液体。
senses.why: Loosening can mean a whole separating into its components.
senses.whyCN: 「松开」也可以指整体分开成各个组成部分。

intro.en: Resolve comes from Latin resolvere, to loosen completely, from re- and solvere, to loosen.
intro.cn: resolve 来自拉丁语 resolvere（彻底解开），由 re- 与 solvere（松开）构成。

items.en: Solvere means to loosen or release.
items.cn: solvere 意为松开、释放。

items.en: Resolvere means to loosen completely or dissolve.
items.cn: resolvere 意为彻底解开或溶解。

items.en: Resolutus is the past participle, loosened or settled.
items.cn: resolutus 是过去分词，意为已解开、已定下。

items.en: Resolver means to resolve or settle.
items.cn: resolver 意为解决、定下。

items.en: Middle English resolven covers solving and deciding.
items.cn: 中古英语 resolven 兼指解决与决定。

items.en: Modern English adds the technical sense of separating into parts.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「分解为部分」的技术义项。

note.en: Resolve is a loosening verb, and it sits near its family and near verbs for solving and deciding.
note.cn: resolve 是一个「松开」动词，与自身词族以及表示解决和决定的动词相邻。

entries.definition: a decision, vote, or solution
entries.definitionCN: 决心；决议；解决

entries.definition: firmly decided
entries.definitionCN: 下定决心的

entries.definition: firm and determined
entries.definitionCN: 坚决的；果断的

entries.definition: to find the answer to a problem

entries.definition: to choose after thinking
entries.definitionCN: 决定

entries.definition: to end a disagreement
entries.definitionCN: 解决；平息

normalIntro.en: Resolve contains solvere, to loosen: solving a problem is loosening a knot.
normalIntro.cn: resolve 含有 solvere（松开）：解决问题就是解开一个结。

normal.en: Re- means back or completely, and solvere means loosen.
normal.cn: re- 表示回或彻底，solvere 表示松开。

normal.en: Resolve a dispute is the common phrase.
normal.cn: resolve a dispute 是常见短语。

normal.en: Resolve to do something means decide firmly.
normal.cn: resolve to do something 意为坚定决定去做。

normal.en: The noun is resolution, the same loosening.
normal.cn: 名词是 resolution，同样是「解开」。

normal.en: Compare solve: solve finds the answer, while resolve often ends a conflict.
normal.cn: 对比 solve：solve 找出答案，resolve 常结束冲突。

abstract.en: Picture a knot loosening under patient fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象绳结在耐心的手指下慢慢松开。

abstract.en: Imagine two people shaking hands after a long argument.
abstract.cn: 想象两人长谈后握手言和。

abstract.en: Think of muddy water settling until it is clear.
abstract.cn: 想象浑水渐渐沉淀变清。

examples.en: The two families resolved their dispute.
examples.cn: 两家人解决了他们的争端。

examples.en: She resolved to speak to him that evening.
examples.cn: 她决心那天晚上和他谈一谈。

examples.en: The mixture resolved into two clear layers.
examples.cn: 混合物分成了两层清澈的液体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + solve」——回头把问题松开、解开，就是解决；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 solvere（松开）→ resolvere（彻底解开）→ 古法语 resolver → 中古英语 resolven → 现代英语 resolve。

sensesIntro.en: The verb loosens a problem, settles a wavering mind, and can also describe a whole separating into layers.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词把问题松开、把摇摆的心思定下，也可描述整体分离成层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knot loosened until the cord lies flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳结被解开，绳子平直。

branches.en: Ending a problem is the core loosening sense.
branches.cn: 结束问题，是核心的「解开」义项。

branches.en: A firm decision settles the mind.
branches.cn: 坚定的决定让心思安定。

branches.en: Separating into parts is a whole coming loose.
branches.cn: 分解成部分，是整体松开。

branches.en: Solving and deciding both remove inner or outer confusion.
branches.cn: 解决与决定都消除内在或外在的混乱。

branches.en: A settled decision and a settled mixture both become clear.
branches.cn: 定下的决定与沉淀的混合物都变得清楚。

intro.en: Resolve is a Latin verb carried through French, with English endings forming its family.
intro.cn: resolve 是经法语传递的拉丁动词，词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin solvere means to loosen, and resolvere means to loosen completely.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 solvere 意为松开，resolvere 意为彻底解开。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of loosening back.
items.exampleCN: re- 增添「往回松开」的意思。

items.example: Resolvere joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: resolvere 把前缀与词根结合。
resolutus 提供「已定下」的含义。

items.example: Resolver carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: resolver 把这个动词带入法语。

items.example: Resolute shares the same Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: resolute 共享同一拉丁词干。

definition_zh: 合作；为共同目标一起行动，也指愿意配合他人的态度
definition_en: the act of working together toward a shared goal, or the willingness to help when asked
core_image: 两个人各抬一端，把同一件重物搬到同一处
scene: 实验室里，两名研究人员一人扶住支架、一人拧紧螺丝，几分钟就把装置装好。 One researcher steadies the frame while the other tightens the bolts, and the job is finished through cooperation.
sceneCN: 这里 cooperation 指「为共同目标一起行动」（第 1 个义项：各方分担同一任务的不同部分）；句意为一名研究者扶住支架、另一名拧紧螺丝，装置靠合作很快装好。图中可辨识物件：支架、螺丝、两只手、装配好的装置。

pos.zh: 合作；协作；配合（不可数；具体合作项目可用复数）

derivatives.zh: 合作；配合
合作的；合作社
合作地
合作者；协作者
合作意愿；配合性

senses.title: Working together toward one goal
senses.definition: the act of working with others toward a shared aim
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起为共同目标做事
senses.example: One researcher steadies the frame while the other tightens the bolts.
senses.exampleCN: 一名研究者扶住支架，另一名拧紧螺丝。
senses.why: co- 'together' plus operari 'to work' says exactly what the word does: two or more agents put their work into one result.
senses.whyCN: co-「一起」加 operari「做事」，正好说出这个词的动作：两个或更多行动者把自己的劳动放进同一个结果。

senses.title: Willingness to help when asked
senses.definition: the readiness to assist someone who asks for help or permission
senses.definitionCN: 愿意帮助提出请求或需要许可的人
senses.example: Thank you for your cooperation during the inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 感谢您在检查期间的配合。
senses.why: the same word names the attitude behind joint work; a request for cooperation asks for access and effort rather than a formal partnership.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也指共同做事背后的态度；请求 cooperation 要的是配合与便利，而不是正式合伙关系。

senses.title: Mutual aid in nature
senses.definition: behavior in which organisms act together in ways that benefit both partners
senses.definitionCN: 生物共同行动、双方都获益的行为
senses.example: Ants and acacia trees cooperate: shelter for defence.
senses.exampleCN: 蚂蚁与金合欢合作：住所换防卫。
senses.why: biology borrowed the word because two species can also divide a job, and the shared benefit is measurable in survival and offspring.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了这个词，因为两个物种也能分担同一件事，而共同收益可以用存活与后代来衡量。

senses.title: Partnership between organizations
senses.definition: joint work between institutions, departments or agencies that keep their own identities
senses.definitionCN: 保持各自身份的机构、部门或机关之间的共同工作
senses.example: The museum works in cooperation with the local school.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆与当地学校合作。
senses.why: organizations cooperate rather than merge; each keeps its boundary but contributes a part, which is why the phrase in cooperation with is so common.
senses.whyCN: 机构是合作而不是合并；各方保留边界却各出一部分，因此「与……合作」这一说法极为常见。

senses.title: International and economic cooperation
senses.definition: coordinated action between countries or firms on trade, aid, research or security
senses.definitionCN: 国家或企业在贸易、援助、研究或安全上的协调行动
senses.example: The two countries signed a cooperation agreement on clean energy.
senses.exampleCN: 两国签署了一项清洁能源合作协议。
senses.why: the modern political sense scales the same division of labour up to states, where no one can compel the other and agreement must be negotiated.
senses.whyCN: 现代政治义把同一种分工放大到国家层面：任何一方都无法强迫对方，合作必须通过协商达成。

senses.title: Coordination of parts in a system
senses.definition: the way parts of a body, machine or system work together so that the whole functions
senses.definitionCN: 身体、机器或系统的各部分协同运作，使整体发挥功能
senses.example: Walking depends on the cooperation of muscles and joints.
senses.exampleCN: 行走依赖肌肉与关节的协同。
senses.why: once the word leaves people, it can describe any set of parts whose combined action produces an effect none could produce alone.
senses.whyCN: 一旦离开人，这个词就能描述任何一组部件：它们的联合动作产生单个部件无法产生的效果。

senses.title: Compliance with authority
senses.titleCN: 对执法或管理方的配合
senses.definition: the act of following instructions or allowing an official procedure to proceed
senses.definitionCN: 遵从指示或允许官方程序顺利进行
senses.example: The driver's cooperation helped the officers clear the road.
senses.exampleCN: 司机的配合帮助警员清理了道路。
senses.why: cooperation here is one-sided compliance; the word softens a demand by presenting it as shared work.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 cooperation 是单方面的顺从；这个词把一项要求说成共同工作，从而缓和了语气。

senses.title: A cooperative strategy in game theory
senses.definition: a strategy in which players choose actions that raise the joint outcome instead of competing for the larger share
senses.definitionCN: 参与者选择提高联合收益、而非争夺更大份额的策略
senses.example: In the repeated game, cooperation pays only if the other side also keeps its promise.
senses.exampleCN: 在重复博弈中，只有当对方也守约时，合作才划算。
senses.why: game theory makes the word technical: cooperation is not goodwill but a strategy that survives only under conditions of repeated contact and observable behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 博弈论把这个词技术化：合作不是善意，而是在重复接触与可观察行为条件下才存活的策略。

intro.en: Cooperation comes from Late Latin cooperari, built on com- 'together' and operari 'to work', itself from opus 'work'. It reached English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cooperation 来自晚期拉丁 cooperari，由 com-「一起」与 operari「做事」构成，而 operari 又源自 opus「工作」。它经法语进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Opus meant 'work, a piece of work'; its stem oper- supplies the verb operari 'to work, labour'.
items.cn: opus 意为「工作、一件作品」；其词干 oper- 构成动词 operari「做事、劳作」。

items.en: Cooperari combined com- 'together' with operari, meaning 'to work together, collaborate'. The prefix assimilated to co- before the vowel.
items.cn: cooperari 把 com-「一起」与 operari 组合，意为「共同做事、协作」；前缀在元音前同化为 co-。

items.en: French coopération carried the noun into English in the sixteenth or seventeenth century; cooperate followed in the same period.
items.cn: 法语 coopération 在 16 或 17 世纪把名词带入英语；动词 cooperate 也在同一时期进入。

items.en: The economic and international senses date mainly from the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, when firms, unions and states began to sign standing agreements.
items.cn: 经济与国际义主要形成于 19 与 20 世纪，当时公司、工会与国家开始签订长期协议。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest English citation of cooperation is not firmly fixed, and dictionaries differ on whether the noun came straight from Latin or through French.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：cooperation 在英语中的最早书证没有确切年代；词典对名词是直接来自拉丁还是经法语而来也有分歧。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same co- plus oper- family; group two holds words that also describe joint work but differ in emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 co- 加 oper- 词族的词；第二组同样描述共同工作，但侧重不同。

entries.definition: Willing to help, or a member-owned business; it describes a quality or an entity, not the activity itself.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意配合的，或成员共有的企业；描述性质或实体，而非活动本身。

entries.definition: To run or work a machine or system; without co- there is no second agent.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机器或运行系统；没有 co- 就没有第二个行动者。

entries.definition: The act of running something, or a surgical procedure; it does not require a partner.
entries.definitionCN: 运行某物，或外科手术；不需要伙伴。

entries.definition: A joint owner; the prefix is the same, but the root is own, not work.
entries.definitionCN: 共同所有人；前缀相同，但词根是 own（拥有），而非 work（工作）。

entries.definition: Working jointly, especially on a creative or intellectual project; it stresses the shared product more than the shared labour.
entries.definitionCN: 共同工作，尤指创意或学术项目；更强调共同成果而非共同劳动。

entries.definition: Organizing separate efforts so that they fit together; cooperation supplies the will, coordination the schedule.
entries.definitionCN: 把各自的努力组织到合适的位置；cooperation 提供意愿，coordination 提供时序。

entries.definition: The combined effort of a team; it is warmer and less formal than cooperation.
entries.definitionCN: 团队的合力；比 cooperation 更口语、更亲切。

entries.definition: A biological relationship in which both species benefit; the technical name for cooperation across species.
entries.definitionCN: 两个物种都获益的生物学关系；是跨物种合作的技术名称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: co- 'together' + operari 'work' = work together; the same root appears in operate and opera.
normal.cn: co-「一起」+ operari「做事」= 共同做事；同一词根也出现在 operate 与 opera 中。

normal.en: The family runs cooperate, cooperative, cooperation, cooperator and cooperatively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cooperate、cooperative、cooperation、cooperator 与 cooperatively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: close cooperation, international cooperation, in cooperation with, full cooperation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：紧密合作、国际合作、与……合作、全力配合。

normal.en: The preposition matters: in cooperation with means two parties, while with the cooperation of means one party assisting another.
normal.cn: 介词很关键：说「与……合作」时指双方，说「在某方的配合下」时指一方协助另一方。

normal.en: Biology has its own word, mutualism, for cooperation between species.
normal.cn: 生物学有专门术语「互利共生」指物种之间的合作。

abstract.en: Picture two people carrying one heavy table, each holding a different end.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人抬一张重桌，各自抓住不同的一端。

abstract.en: Picture a rowing crew whose oars enter the water on the same beat.
abstract.cn: 想象赛艇队员的桨在同一拍入水。

abstract.en: Picture a machine whose parts each do one motion so that the whole moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器，每个部件各做一个动作，整体才动起来。

examples.en: The project succeeded through close cooperation between the two labs.
examples.cn: 这个项目靠两个实验室的紧密合作而成功。

examples.en: Police thanked the public for its cooperation during the search.
examples.cn: 警方感谢公众在搜寻期间的配合。

examples.en: Clean-energy cooperation between the two countries began in the 1990s.
examples.cn: 两国的清洁能源合作始于 20 世纪 90 年代。

dict_mnemonic.text: co（一起）+ operation（操作）——几个人一起操作同一件事 → 合作

root: 拉丁晚期 cooperari「共同做事」= com-（一起）+ operari「工作」（源自 opus「工作」）。英语经法语借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep the same division of labour but change the setting: a task, a request, a species pair, two institutions, two states, a body's parts, an authority, a game.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项保持同一种分工，只更换场景：一项任务、一次请求、一对物种、两个机构、两个国家、身体各部、一个执法方、一场博弈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one load, two pairs of hands, each taking a different end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件重物，两双手，各自抬住不同的一端。

branches.en: THE CORE: a shared aim is what turns separate efforts into one act.
branches.cn: 核心：共同目标把分散的努力变成同一个动作。

branches.en: THE ATTITUDE: willingness is the door through which help enters.
branches.cn: 态度：意愿是帮助得以进入的那道门。

branches.en: ACROSS SPECIES: biology measures the shared benefit in survival.
branches.cn: 跨物种：生物学用存活来衡量共同收益。

branches.en: ACROSS BORDERS: institutions and states cooperate without merging.
branches.cn: 跨越边界：机构与国家合作而不合并。

branches.en: OTHER SHAPES: parts, compliance and strategy all keep the same division of labour.
branches.cn: 其他形态：部件、顺从与策略都保持同一种分工。

intro.en: Cooperation is a prefix-root noun: co- 'together' plus operari 'to work' plus -ation. The same root family runs through operate, operation and opera.
intro.cn: cooperation 是前缀加词根的名词：co-「一起」加 operari「做事」，再加 -ation。同一词根族贯穿 operate、operation 与 opera。

latinIntro.en: Latin opus 'work' gives operari and, with com-, cooperari; English takes cooperate, cooperation, cooperative and cooperator from this line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 opus「工作」生成 operari，并与 com- 合成 cooperari；英语由此得到 cooperate、cooperation、cooperative 与 cooperator。

items.example: Before a vowel the prefix shortens to co-.
items.exampleCN: 在元音前这个前缀缩为 co-。

items.example: Opus is the noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: opus 是整个词族背后的名词。

items.example: Operari supplies the verbal idea of labour.
items.exampleCN: operari 提供「劳作」的动词含义。

items.example: The Late Latin verb named joint labour.
items.exampleCN: 这个晚期拉丁动词命名共同劳动。
cooperari 加 -ation 命名这项活动。
合作需要一个共同目标。

items.example: The two teams agreed to cooperate.

items.meaning: tending to work together; a jointly owned business
items.meaningCN: 倾向于合作的；共同所有的企业
items.example: A cooperative shop is owned by its members.
items.exampleCN: 合作社商店由成员共有。

items.example: Every cooperator received a share of the harvest.

scene: 这台新机器让我们能更快完成工作。 The new machine enables us to work faster.

senses.title: To make someone able
senses.definition: to give someone the means or ability to do something
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人做某事的手段或能力
senses.example: The scholarship enabled her to study abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 奖学金使她能够出国留学。
senses.why: The prefix en- puts ability into the person, so the word names the removal of a limit.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 把能力放入一个人身上，因此这个词命名限制的解除。

senses.title: To make something possible
senses.definition: to create the conditions in which an event or process can happen
senses.definitionCN: 创造使某个事件或过程得以发生的条件
senses.example: Good roads enable trade.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的道路使贸易成为可能。
senses.why: Conditions act like keys, so the word also covers making events possible.
senses.whyCN: 条件就像钥匙，因此这个词也涵盖让事件成为可能。

senses.title: To switch a function on
senses.definition: to turn on a feature or setting in a device or program
senses.definitionCN: 打开设备或程序中的某项功能或设置
senses.example: Enable the timer before you start.
senses.exampleCN: 开始前请启用计时器。
senses.why: A feature that is off cannot act, so switching it on is a technical kind of enabling.
senses.whyCN: 关闭的功能无法发挥作用，因此打开它也是一种技术意义上的使能。

definition_zh: 比例；部分；份额；均衡；相称；（数学）比例式；大小、规模
definition_en: the relation between parts, or between a part and the whole, in size, amount, or importance
core_image: 一块蛋糕被切成大小不同的几份，每一份与整块之间都有固定的比
scene: 建筑师在图纸上反复比较窗户与墙面。 If the window is too large the wall looks light and unstable, so the proportion of glass to brick has to be judged by eye.
sceneCN: 这里 proportion 是「比例、相称」（第 2 个义项：各部之间在大小上的关系）；句意：窗太大墙面就显得轻浮不稳，所以玻璃与砖的比例只能靠眼睛来把握。图中可辨识物件：建筑立面图、窗户、墙面分区、比例尺、铅笔；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A part relative to the whole
senses.definition: a part considered in relation to the whole amount
senses.definitionCN: 相对于整体而言的一部分
senses.example: A large proportion of students commute.
senses.exampleCN: 很大比例的学生通勤。
senses.why: Latin proportio joins pro- 'according to' to portio 'share'. The word begins with shares: one part measured against the whole it belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proportio 把 pro-“按照”与 portio“份额”结合。这个词始于份额：一部分相对于它所属的整体被衡量。

senses.title: The relation between parts
senses.definition: the comparative size or amount of two or more parts
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个部分在大小或数量上的对比关系
senses.example: The proportion of sugar to flour matters.
senses.exampleCN: 糖与面粉的比例很关键。
senses.why: Two parts can be compared without a whole: this is the relational core. Cooking, chemistry, and design all depend on the ratio between ingredients.
senses.whyCN: 两部分可以脱离整体比较：这是关系性的核心。烹饪、化学与设计都依赖配料之间的比率。

senses.title: Correct balance or harmony
senses.definition: the quality of parts fitting together well
senses.definitionCN: 各部分彼此协调得当的性质
senses.example: The room has a pleasing sense of proportion.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间有种悦目的比例感。
senses.why: Aesthetics evaluates the relation: some ratios look right, others jar. Proportion becomes a judgment, not just a measurement.
senses.whyCN: 美学评估这种关系：某些比率看起来对，另一些则刺眼。proportion 于是成了判断，而不只是测量。

senses.title: An equal share (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, a share allotted to each person
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：分给每个人的一份
senses.example: Each heir received a proportion of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 每位继承人分得遗产的一份。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the simple share: portio is a portion. The mathematical sense grew from comparing such shares.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是简单的份额：portio 就是一份。数学义从比较这些份额生长出来。

senses.title: An equation of ratios (mathematics)
senses.definition: a statement that two ratios are equal
senses.definitionCN: 两个比率相等的陈述
senses.example: Solve the proportion 3/4 = x/12.
senses.why: Mathematics formalizes the comparison: a proportion asserts an equality between two ratios. The word keeps its 'share' root even in algebra.
senses.whyCN: 数学把比较形式化：比例式断言两个比率的相等。即使在代数中，这个词仍保留“份额”词根。

senses.title: Direct or inverse proportion
senses.definition: a relationship in which one quantity changes at a fixed rate with another
senses.definitionCN: 一个量随另一个量按固定比率变化的关系
senses.example: Speed is in direct proportion to distance over time.
senses.exampleCN: 速度与距离除以时间成正比。
senses.why: Science uses proportion for lawful co-variation: as one rises, the other rises or falls by a fixed factor. The ratio becomes a law of nature.
senses.whyCN: 科学用 proportion 指有规律的共变：一个上升，另一个按固定倍数上升或下降。比率成了自然法则。

senses.title: Size or dimensions
senses.definition: the size or scale of something, especially its relative dimensions
senses.definitionCN: 某物的大小或尺度，尤指相对维度
senses.example: The sculpture has heroic proportions.
senses.exampleCN: 这座雕塑体量宏伟。
senses.why: Proportions in the plural name the measured dimensions of a body or building. The relation becomes the thing itself: a person of large proportions.
senses.whyCN: 复数 proportions 命名身体或建筑被量出的维度。关系变成了事物本身：a person of large proportions。

senses.title: Proportional representation
senses.definition: an electoral system in which seats are allotted in proportion to votes
senses.definitionCN: 按得票比例分配席位的选举制度
senses.example: The party favors proportional representation.
senses.exampleCN: 该党支持比例代表制。
senses.why: Politics applies the ratio to power: votes are shares, and seats should mirror them. The word becomes a principle of fairness.
senses.whyCN: 政治把比率用于权力：选票是份额，席位应映照它们。这个词成了一种公平原则。

senses.title: Analogy or relation (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, a correspondence or analogy between things
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：事物之间的对应或类比关系
senses.example: The proportion between microcosm and macrocosm was a medieval theme.
senses.exampleCN: 小宇宙与大宇宙的对应是中世纪的主题。
senses.why: Old philosophy used proportion for cosmic correspondences, not just numbers. The word could mean 'analogy', which is why proportionality once carried metaphysical weight.
senses.whyCN: 旧哲学用 proportion 指宇宙对应，而非只是数字。这个词曾可指“类比”，所以 proportional 一度带有形而上学分量。

intro.en: Proportion is a share word before it is a math word. Latin proportio joins pro- 'according to' with portio 'share', so it names the relation between allotments. Mathematics later made that relation exact.
intro.cn: proportion 先是份额词，然后才是数学词。拉丁语 proportio 把 pro-“按照”与 portio“份额”结合，因此它命名分配物之间的关系。数学后来把这种关系精确化。

items.en: First recorded as 'relation, correspondence, comparative share', from Latin proportio.
items.cn: 最早记录为“关系、对应、比较中的份额”，来自拉丁语 proportio。

items.en: proportio(nem) 'comparative relation, analogy' = pro- 'according to, for' + portio 'a share, a part'.
items.cn: proportio(nem)“比较关系、类比”= pro-“按照、为了”+ portio“份额、部分”。

items.en: portio 'a share' also gives portion, apportion, and proportion. The family is about dividing something into parts.
items.cn: portio“份额”还生成 portion、apportion、proportion。这个词族关乎把某物分成部分。

items.en: Here pro- does not mean 'forward' as in proceed or project; it means 'according to, in relation to'. The same prefix has several senses.
items.cn: 此处 pro- 不表示 proceed 或 project 中的“向前”，而表示“按照、相对于”。同一前缀有多种含义。

items.en: The mathematical and aesthetic senses become precise: proportion in geometry, and proportion in art and architecture.
items.cn: 数学与美学义变得精确：几何中的比例，以及艺术与建筑中的比例。

items.en: Modern English uses proportion for shares, ratios, balance, size, and electoral systems, all tracing back to portio.
items.cn: 现代英语用 proportion 指份额、比率、均衡、规模与选举制度，全部追溯到 portio。

note.en: The first group shares the portio stem; the second is about nouns that also mean a ratio or a share.
note.cn: 第一组共享 portio 词干，第二组看同样表示“比率”或“份额”的名词。

entries.definition: a share or piece of something. It is the simple noun behind proportion.
entries.definitionCN: 一份或一块。它是 proportion 背后的简单名词。

entries.definition: changing at a fixed ratio with something else.
entries.definitionCN: 与某物按固定比率变化的。

entries.definition: to divide and distribute shares. It is ad- 'to' + portio.

entries.definition: the numerical relation between two quantities. It is the measured form of proportion.
entries.definitionCN: 两个数量之间的数值关系。它是 proportion 的测量形式。

entries.definition: a portion given to one person. It names the piece, not the relation between pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 分给一个人的一份。它命名那块，而非块与块的关系。

entries.definition: an even distribution of parts or forces. It matches the aesthetic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 部分或力量的均衡分布。它对应美学义。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin portio 'share', pro- 'according to', the portion/apportion family, and the phrases in proportion to and out of proportion.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 portio“份额”、pro-“按照”、portion/apportion 词族，以及 in proportion to / out of proportion 两个短语。

normal.en: Portio means 'share'. Proportion is the relation between shares: this part against that part, or part against whole.
normal.cn: portio 意为“份额”。proportion 是份额之间的关系：这份对那份，或部分对整体。

normal.en: Here pro- means 'according to', not 'forward'. Proportion is measured according to the shares.
normal.cn: 此处 pro- 意为“按照”，不是“向前”。proportion 是按份额来衡量的。

normal.en: In proportion to means a fixed ratio holds; out of proportion means the ratio has broken, often in emotion.
normal.cn: in proportion to 意为固定比率成立；out of proportion 意为比率破裂，常用于情绪。

normal.en: A sense of proportion is a sense of relative size: knowing what matters how much.
normal.cn: a sense of proportion 是对相对大小的感觉：知道什么值多少。

normal.en: Proportional representation makes seats mirror votes: the political version of the same ratio.
normal.cn: 比例代表制让席位映照选票：同一比率在政治中的版本。

abstract.en: Proportion is how meaning is made from relation: nothing is large or small except against something else.
abstract.cn: 比例是从关系生成意义的方式：没有东西是大或小，除非相对他物。

abstract.en: A sense of proportion is a moral skill as much as an aesthetic one: it is knowing what deserves how much attention.
abstract.cn: 分寸感既是审美技能也是道德技能：知道什么该得到多少注意。

abstract.en: The word moves from shares to ratios to justice: fair distribution and exact measurement share one root.
abstract.cn: 这个词从份额走到比率再走到正义：公平分配与精确测量共享一个词根。

examples.en: The proportion of women in the workforce has risen.
examples.cn: 女性在劳动力中的比例上升了。

examples.en: Try to keep the problem in proportion.
examples.cn: 尽量把问题看得合乎分寸。

examples.en: The two quantities are in direct proportion.
examples.cn: 这两个量成正比。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若剖身”——把整体扑开、剖开身子分成几份 → proportion 比例、份额

root: 拉丁语 proportio“比较关系”，由 pro-“按照”+ portio“份额”构成；portio 还生成 portion、apportion。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of proportion, all resting on a share. The share can be compared to the whole, to another share, to an ideal balance, to a mathematical law, to a body's size, or to a vote.
sensesIntro.cn: proportion 的九个义项都建立在“份额”上。这个份额可以相对整体、相对另一份、相对理想均衡、相对数学规律、相对身体大小，或相对选票。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: parts measured against one another and against the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：各部分彼此衡量，也与整体衡量。

branches.en: SHARE: one part set against the whole, or allotted to one person.
branches.cn: 份额：一部分相对整体，或分给一个人。

branches.en: RATIO: parts compared with each other, in arithmetic and in natural law.
branches.cn: 比率：部分彼此比较，在算术与自然法则中皆然。

branches.en: BALANCE: the relation judged as harmonious or fitting.
branches.cn: 均衡：这种关系被判断为和谐、得当。

branches.en: SIZE AND ANALOGY: measured dimensions, and the older idea of correspondence.
branches.cn: 大小与类比：被量出的维度，以及较早的对应观念。

branches.en: POLITICS: seats allotted in proportion to votes, making the ratio a rule of justice.
branches.cn: 政治：席位按选票比例分配，使比率成为正义规则。

intro.en: Proportion is a noun from Latin proportio. English adds -al, -ate, -ality, and the negative dis-, while portio also gives portion and apportion.
intro.cn: proportion 是来自拉丁 proportio 的名词。英语加 -al、-ate、-ality 与否定 dis-，portio 还生成 portion 与 apportion。

latinIntro.en: Latin proportio 'comparative relation' joins pro- 'according to' with portio 'share'. The portio family is about dividing into parts, which is why the word can mean both a ratio and a fair share.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proportio“比较关系”把 pro-“按照”与 portio“份额”结合。portio 词族关乎分成部分，所以这个词既能指比率，也能指公平份额。

normalIntro.cn: host 指迎接、组织或提供场所的一方。

normal.en: The host welcomed every guest warmly tonight.
normal.cn: 今晚的主人热情地欢迎每一位客人。

normal.en: Our host showed us to the dining room.
normal.cn: 主人把我们带到餐厅。

normal.en: She was the host of the evening show.
normal.cn: 她是晚间节目的主持人。

normal.en: The city will host the games next year.

abstract.en: The word quietly spreads from homes to shows to cells.

definition_zh: 合理的；公道的；还算好的
definition_en: sensible and fair, based on good reason; fair in price; moderate in amount and acceptable
core_image: 天平两端重量相当，指针停在正中
scene: 天平两端的重量差不多，指针稳稳停在正中。 The hotel charges a reasonable price for the room.
sceneCN: 这里 reasonable 是「公道的」（第 2 个义项：价格公平、不离谱）；句意为这家酒店的房间价格公道。画面里可留意：平衡的天平、停在正中的指针、价目牌。

pos.zh: 合理的；公道的；还算好的

derivatives.zh: reasonable 的词根，指理由、理性
reasonable 加 -ly，指合理地、相当地
reason 加 -ing，指推理
un- 与 reasonable 复合，指不合理的

senses.title: Sensible and fair
senses.definition: based on good reason and fair to those involved
senses.definitionCN: 基于充分理由，且对相关各方公平
senses.example: She gave a reasonable explanation for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 她为延误给出了合理的解释。
senses.why: Reasonable is reason plus -able, so it describes what can be supported by reason and accepted as fair.
senses.whyCN: reasonable 是 reason 加 -able，描述能被理由支持、并被接受为公平的事物。

senses.title: Fair in price
senses.definition: of a price, not too high and fair for what is offered
senses.definitionCN: 指价格不过高，与所提供之物相称
senses.example: The hotel charges a reasonable price for the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店的房间价格公道。
senses.why: A price that reason can approve is one that is not excessive, so the word came to mean fair in price.
senses.whyCN: 理性能够认可的价格，就是不过分的价格，于是这个词引申为「价格公道」。

senses.title: Moderate and acceptable
senses.definition: of an amount, moderate but enough to be acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 指数量适中但足以令人接受
senses.example: There was a reasonable amount of time to finish the work.
senses.exampleCN: 完成这项工作有相当充裕的时间。
senses.why: What stays within reason is neither tiny nor excessive, so the word marks a moderate amount that still satisfies.
senses.whyCN: 合乎理性之物既不过小也不过量，因此这个词标记一个适中却仍令人满意的数量。

intro.en: Reasonable is reason plus the ending -able, meaning able to be supported by reason; reason itself goes back to Latin ratio.
intro.cn: reasonable 是 reason 加词尾 -able，意为能被理由支持的；reason 本身可追溯到拉丁语 ratio。

items.en: Ratio meant reckoning and reason, the standard against which a claim is judged.
items.cn: ratio 意为计算与理性，是评判一个说法的标准。

items.en: English reason carries both the cause behind a thing and the mind's power of judging.
items.cn: 英语 reason 既承载事物背后的原因，也承载心智的判断力。

items.en: The ending -able means able to be, so reason plus -able is able to be justified by reason.
items.cn: 词尾 -able 意为「能被……的」，因此 reason 加 -able 就是「能被理性证明的」。

items.en: A sum that reason approves is fair, and an amount that reason accepts is moderate.
items.cn: 理性认可的数额是公道的，理性接受的数量是适中的。

items.en: Modern English uses reasonable for fair judgment, fair prices, and moderate but acceptable amounts.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reasonable 指公平的判断、公道的价格，以及适中却可接受的数量。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the reason root; the near-meaning group gathers words for fairness and moderation.
note.cn: 形近组收 reason 词根的词；近义组收表示公平与适中的词。

normalIntro.en: The word asks whether reason can approve: a fair judgment, a fair price, and a moderate amount all pass that test.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词问的是理性能否认可：公平的判断、公道的价格、适中的数量都能通过这一检验。

normal.en: Reasonable is reason plus -able, so it means able to be justified by reason.
normal.cn: reasonable 是 reason 加 -able，意为能被理性证明的。

normal.en: A reasonable price is one that does not ask too much.
normal.cn: 公道的价格，是不过分索价的价格。

normal.en: A reasonable explanation is one that holds together and is fair.
normal.cn: 合理的解释，是前后一致且公平的解释。

normal.en: Be reasonable about a delay means do not react with anger.
normal.cn: be reasonable about a delay 意为不要动怒。

normal.en: Unreasonable is the opposite, built with the negative prefix un-.
normal.cn: unreasonable 是反义词，由否定前缀 un- 构成。

abstract.en: Reasonable is the meeting point of logic and fairness.
abstract.cn: reasonable 是逻辑与公平的交汇处。

abstract.en: What is reasonable to one person may still be too much for another.
abstract.cn: 对一个人合理的，对另一个人也许仍然过分。

abstract.en: To be reasonable is to leave room for the other side.

examples.en: There was a reasonable amount of time to finish the work.

root: 拉丁语 reri（计算）→ ratio（理性）→ 古法语 reisun → 英语 reason + 后缀 -able → reasonable；同族有 reasonably、unreasonable。

definition_zh: 联想；把……联系起来；交往；同事
definition_en: to connect things in the mind, to spend time with people, or a person you work with
core_image: 两条原本分开的线在脑中打了一个结
scene: 一闻到消毒水味，她就想起医院。 That smell is associated with the hospital.
sceneCN: 这里 associate 是「联想到」（第 1 个义项：把两件事在脑中连起来）；句意是那股气味让人联想到医院。

senses.title: Connect in the mind
senses.definition: to connect one thing with another in your mind
senses.definitionCN: 在头脑中把一件事与另一件事连起来
senses.example: That smell is associated with the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 那股气味让人联想到医院。
senses.why: Associate comes from Latin associare, 'to join as a companion', built on socius 'companion', so the core act is pairing two things so that one calls up the other.
senses.whyCN: associate 源自拉丁语 associare「使结为同伴」，词基 socius 意为同伴，所以核心动作是把两样东西配成伴，见到一个就想起另一个。

senses.title: Spend time with people
senses.definition: to spend time with a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 与某人或某群体经常相处
senses.example: He associates with artists and writers.
senses.exampleCN: 他常与画家和作家来往。
senses.why: When the companionship is between people rather than ideas, the same joining becomes the plain act of keeping company with a group.
senses.whyCN: 当「结伴」发生在人与人之间而不是概念之间时，同一个连接动作就落成了与某群人来往这一日常含义。

senses.title: Work partner
senses.definition: a person you work or do business with
senses.definitionCN: 一起工作或做生意的人
senses.example: She met a business associate at the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 她在机场见了一位生意伙伴。
senses.why: The noun form names the companion who has been joined to you by work, so it covers colleagues and business partners without implying friendship.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指因工作而与你结伴的人，因此既能指同事，也能指生意伙伴，并不暗示私人交情。

intro.en: Associate is built on the Latin word for a companion, and its senses all keep the idea of joining.
intro.cn: associate 建立在拉丁语「同伴」一词上，各义项都保留「结成伴」的意思。

items.en: English associate covered both company and mental linking.

items.en: The noun sense 'colleague' settled in business use.

definition_zh: 插头；塞子；插上电源；堵塞；插入
definition_en: a small device with metal pins that connects a wire to an electrical socket; a piece of material that blocks a hole; to connect an appliance to power or push something firmly in; and to block an opening or a gap
core_image: 一只手把橡胶塞按进瓶口，另一只手把插头推向插座
scene: 浴缸里的水一直往下漏，修理工蹲下来查看排水口。 He pulled the plug out of the bath and watched the water drain away.
sceneCN: 这里 plug 是「塞子」（第 2 个义项：堵住孔洞的东西）；句意为他拔掉浴缸的塞子，看着水流走。图中可辨识物件：浴缸、排水口、橡胶塞。

derivatives.zh: 由否定前缀 un- 加 plug 构成，义为「拔掉插头；断开电源」
由 plug 双写末尾的 g 加 -er 构成，义为「塞东西的人；埋头苦干的人」
由动词短语 plug in 加连字符凝固而成，义为「插件；插入式装置」

senses.title: An electrical connector with metal pins
senses.definition: a small device with metal pins that joins a wire or an appliance to an electrical socket
senses.definitionCN: 带金属插脚的小装置，把电线或电器接到电源插座上
senses.example: The plug does not fit this socket.
senses.exampleCN: 这个插头跟这个插座不配套。
senses.why: The electrical sense is a later use of the older stopper: the plug is pushed into a socket exactly as a bung is pushed into a hole, and it is the tight fit that carries the current.
senses.whyCN: 插头这个义项是较晚从「塞子」引申出来的：插头被推进插座，正像塞子被推进孔里，正是这种严丝合缝的嵌入把电流接通。

senses.title: A piece of material that blocks a hole
senses.definition: a piece of rubber, wood or cork used to close a hole, especially in a bath, sink or barrel
senses.definitionCN: 用来堵住孔洞的橡胶、木头或软木块，尤指浴缸、水槽或桶上的
senses.example: He pulled the plug out of the bath and watched the water drain away.
senses.exampleCN: 他拔掉浴缸的塞子，看着水流走。
senses.why: This is the earliest English sense, taken from Dutch: a shaped piece forced into an opening so that nothing passes. Every later use of the word is a version of that tight fit.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最早的义项，借自荷兰语：一块成形的东西被硬塞进开口，让任何东西都过不去。这个词后来的用法，都是这种「嵌紧」的变体。

senses.title: To push in or connect to power
senses.definition: to push something firmly into an opening, or to connect an appliance to electricity by means of a plug
senses.definitionCN: 把某物用力推进开口，或通过插头把电器接通电源
senses.example: She plugged the heater into the wall and turned it on.
senses.exampleCN: 她把取暖器插到墙上，然后打开。
senses.why: The verb performs the noun: to plug is to behave like a plug, driving a shaped end into a matching hole until it holds. Electricity turned that motion into the everyday way of giving a machine power.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的动作做出来：plug 一样东西，就是像塞子那样把成形的末端推进相配的孔，直到卡住。电的出现让这个动作成了给机器供电的日常方式。

senses.title: To block an opening or a gap
senses.definition: to fill a hole, a leak or a gap so that nothing can pass through it
senses.definitionCN: 把孔洞、漏洞或缺口填住，使任何东西都无法通过
senses.example: They plugged the leak with a strip of cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用一条布堵住了漏水处。
senses.why: A plug stops flow by occupying the opening, so the verb extends from forcing in a stopper to any act of filling a gap, including plugging a hole in a budget or in an argument.
senses.whyCN: 塞子靠占住开口来阻断流动，所以动词从「塞入塞子」扩展到任何填补缺口的动作，包括补上预算或论证里的漏洞。

intro.en: Plug is a Germanic borrowing from Middle Dutch, where it named a block or a bung; its deeper origin is uncertain, and English first used it for a stopper before it named an electrical connector.
intro.cn: plug 是从中古荷兰语借来的日耳曼词，原指木块或桶塞；更早的来源不确定，英语先用它指塞子，后来才指电插头。

items.en: Middle Dutch plugge named a block or a bung, a shaped piece used to stop a hole; the deeper origin of the form is uncertain.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 plugge 指木块或桶塞，即用来堵孔的成形木块；这个形式更早的来源不确定。

items.en: English borrowed plug in the seventeenth century for a stopper in a barrel, a bath or a pipe.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 plug，指桶、浴缸或管道里的塞子。

items.en: The word widened to any blocking piece, and the verb appeared for stopping a hole or a leak.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何起堵塞作用的东西，动词也出现了，表示堵住孔洞或漏洞。

items.en: When wires needed joints, the shaped metal connector that fitted into a socket was called a plug, by analogy with a bung.
items.cn: 当电线需要接头时，那种嵌进插座的成形金属连接件被叫作 plug，这是类比桶塞而来的。

items.en: Modern English adds plug in, unplug and the informal sense of promoting something by repeating its name.
items.cn: 现代英语又加上 plug in、unplug，以及反复提名字来宣传某物的口语义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's own derivatives and compounds; the near-meaning group gathers objects and verbs for stopping or joining a hole.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词自己的派生词与复合词；近义组收堵孔、接孔一类的物件与动词。

entries.definition: To disconnect an appliance by pulling out its plug.
entries.definitionCN: 拔掉插头，使电器断电。

entries.definition: A person who plugs something, or who works steadily at a task.
entries.definitionCN: 塞东西的人，或埋头苦干的人。

entries.definition: A small module or program that is connected into a larger system.
entries.definitionCN: 接入更大系统的小模块或程序；插件。

entries.definition: The hole in a bath or sink that a plug closes.
entries.definitionCN: 浴缸或水槽里由塞子堵住的排水孔。

entries.definition: An object pushed into the neck of a bottle to close it.
entries.definitionCN: 塞进瓶口使其封闭的物件。

entries.definition: A round piece of wood or rubber that closes the hole of a barrel.
entries.definitionCN: 封住桶口的圆形木塞或橡胶塞。

entries.definition: The fitting in a wall that receives a plug.
entries.definitionCN: 墙上承接插头的插座。

entries.definition: To stop something passing through an opening.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某物通过开口；堵塞。

normalIntro.en: The word arrived from Dutch as a shaped stopper, and the whole family keeps the picture of something pressed tightly into a hole.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从荷兰语进来时就是一块成形的塞子，整个词族都带着「紧紧压进孔里」的画面。

normal.en: Middle Dutch plugge meant a block or a bung, so the bath plug is closer to the original sense than the electrical plug.
normal.cn: 中古荷兰语 plugge 意为木块或桶塞，所以浴缸塞子比电插头更接近本义。

normal.en: The electrical plug is named by analogy: metal pins are pressed into a socket the way a bung is pressed into a barrel.
normal.cn: 电插头是类比得名：金属插脚被压进插座，正如桶塞被压进桶口。

normal.en: Unplug adds the reversing prefix un- and means to take the plug out, cutting the current.
normal.cn: unplug 加了表示相反动作的前缀 un-，意为拔出插头、切断电流。

normal.en: Plug the gap keeps the old physical idea: something is put into an opening so that nothing slips through.
normal.cn: plug the gap 保留了古老的实物想法：把东西放进缺口，让任何东西都漏不过去。

normal.en: Plug-in is written with a hyphen as a noun, and the same two words without a hyphen form the verb phrase plug in.
normal.cn: plug-in 作名词时带连字符；同样两个词不带连字符时则是动词短语 plug in。

abstract.en: A plug is a small object whose whole purpose is to be exactly the wrong shape for the hole it fills.
abstract.cn: 塞子的全部用处，就是恰好以不合适的形状占满它填的孔。

abstract.en: Electricity turned a bung into a bridge: the same tight fit now carries power instead of stopping water.
abstract.cn: 电把桶塞变成了桥：同样的紧密嵌合，如今输送电力而不是拦住水。

abstract.en: To plug a gap is to admit that a system has a hole and to decide it must not be seen.
abstract.cn: 填补缺口，就是承认系统有个洞，并决定不让它被看见。

examples.en: The plug does not fit this socket.
examples.cn: 这个插头跟这个插座不配套。

examples.en: He pulled the plug out of the bath and watched the water drain away.
examples.cn: 他拔掉浴缸的塞子，看着水流走。

examples.en: They plugged the leak with a strip of cloth.
examples.cn: 他们用一条布堵住了漏水处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「噗嗤」——塞子塞进瓶口发出噗嗤一声；记住 plug 是塞子，也是插头。

root: 中古荷兰语 plugge（木块、桶塞）借入英语为 plug，更早来源不确定：先指塞子，十九世纪后类比桶塞，指嵌入插座的金属插头，再引申出插入、堵塞等动词义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a shaped piece pressed into an opening; the senses run from the stopper, to the electrical connector that copies it, to the act of connecting, and finally to the act of blocking a gap.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一块被压进开口的成形物件；义项从塞子，走到模仿它的电插头，再到接通电源的动作，最后落到堵住缺口的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rubber bung forced into a bottle mouth, and a hand pushing a plug toward a socket.
core.cn: 核心意象：橡胶塞被按进瓶口，另一只手把插头推向插座。

branches.en: a plug pushed into a wall socket
branches.cn: 插头推进墙上插座

branches.en: a rubber bung in a bath drain
branches.cn: 浴缸排水口里的橡胶塞

branches.en: a heater coming alive at the wall
branches.cn: 取暖器在插座上亮起

branches.en: a cloth stuffed into a leaking pipe
branches.cn: 布团塞进漏水的管子

branches.en: a gap in a budget being filled
branches.cn: 预算缺口被补上

intro.en: The word is a Dutch borrowing of a stopper, and English builds its family with a reversing prefix, an agent suffix and compounds made from the verb phrase.
intro.cn: 这个词是借自荷兰语的「塞子」，英语用表示相反动作的前缀、表示施动者的后缀，以及由动词短语凝固成的复合词来扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; it came into English from Middle Dutch, and the further origin of the Dutch noun is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它从中古荷兰语进入英语，而那个荷兰语名词更早的来源不确定。

senses.why: The word also means not hollow or mixed.

items.en: Solidus meant firm, whole, or undivided.
items.cn: solidus 意为坚固、完整或不可分割的。

items.en: Solide kept the sense of firmness.
items.cn: solide 保留了坚固的意思。

items.en: The word entered English as solid.
items.cn: 这个词以 solid 进入英语。

items.en: Science used it for matter that keeps its shape.
items.cn: 科学用它指保持形状的物质。

items.en: It also came to mean reliable or pure.
items.cn: 它也开始表示可靠的或纯的。

entries.definition: only or single

abstract.en: What is whole cannot be hollow.
